summary: No new candidate. I derived the invariants of the rollup shell (DaveConsensus, InputBox, Application, DaveAppFactory, ApplicationFactory, MultiLevelTournamentFactory, and the validity-proof libraries of cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10) from the released sources and attacked each one by reading and by one experiment. Every invariant held, or failed only in a way that is already listed in context.md (R1-A5-1, R1-A5-2, R1-A7-2, R8-GOALEPOCH-2, R8-GOALOUTPUT-1, R8-GOALOUTPUT-2, R8-GOALNODE-1, R8-GOALNOPROOF-1). I did not re-report those.
invariants_checked_no_candidate: I1 Each input belongs to exactly one epoch, in order. DaveConsensus keeps [lower, upper); acceptStagedTournamentResult sets lower := upper and upper := lower + min(pending, 2^24); the constructor does the same from 0. InputBox arrays only grow, so ranges are contiguous, disjoint and capped (A3). Under DaveAppFactory epoch 0 is always empty: the application is created and the consensus constructed in one call with no untrusted call between them, and InputBox.addInput reverts with ApplicationNotDeployed for an address without code.

I2 Input bytes are the on-chain record (A3). provideMerkleRootOfInput requires keccak256(input) == InputBox.getInputHash(app, lower + i), so the root and the length that CartesiStateTransition passes to SendCmioResponse are bound byte for byte; index >= upper returns zero and CartesiStateTransition then requires an empty witness. The provider reads the current bounds, not those of the calling tournament: I confirmed this is harmless, because a root with a sealed inner match has matchCount > 0 and cannot be staged, and every operation of a finished tournament reverts with TournamentIsFinished, so no leaf match of epoch N can run after epoch N+1 is sealed.

I3 The state an epoch starts from is the one the previous epoch settled (A1). The next root is instantiated with the staged finalMachineStateHash in the same transaction that records it. Staged values have one write path: tournamentStanding() == ROOT_WINNER of the tournament this contract created, whose finalState was authenticated at join as the last leaf with exactly `height` siblings (A2). A root standing cannot change after it is finished (joins closed, matchCount == 0, every mutator gated by !_isFinished).

I4 An outputs root is recorded only for an accepted-yield settled state (A5). LibMachineValidityProof proves three leaves against the same root with 59 siblings each: iflags_Y (0x308) != 0, htif_tohost (0x330) with dev == yield, cmd == manual, reason == rx-accepted, and the first tx-buffer word (0x60800000). The predicate is the same as the one send_cmio_response uses for an applicable advance delivery (src/send-cmio-response.cpp, isYieldedManualWith in src/uarch-solidity-compat.hpp), and the step-0.15.0 constants it is compiled with equal the in-tree emulator's (checked with the built Lua module: iflags_Y 0x308, htif_tohost 0x330, tx buffer 0x60800000, word 2^5, root 2^64, outputs 2^63). The byte offset arithmetic of getBytes8FromBytes32AtOffset (offset << 3 bits) is right for both registers. Halt, exception, any other manual reason and a stop at imcyclemax without a yield cannot pass. A rejected last input settles the pre-input state, which passes.

I5 An output executes at most once and only against a recorded root. Application.executeOutput validates keccak256(output) at proof.outputIndex with exactly 63 siblings (index >> 63 must be 0), asks the validator, then sets a global bitmap bit before the call; a failed call reverts the whole transaction, so the bit is not consumed. Fixed heights rule out leaf/inner-node confusion (a 64-byte output equal to two child hashes would need a 64-level path). Roots are write-once and never removed; migrateToOutputsMerkleRootValidator is owner-only and deployment-block-only, and DaveAppFactory renounces ownership in the same call. isOutputsMerkleRootValid is bound to the one application.

I6 Staging, sentries, foreclosure. Stage needs the current epoch number, no staged result, ROOT_WINNER and a valid proof; accept needs a staged result and either unanimity of all sentry slots on the staged hash or the staging period. Sentry claims are per slot per epoch and only compared with the staged hash, so they can shorten but not change the result. All four mutators are gated by notForeclosed. Refund (index >= lower) and withdrawal (last finalized machine root, template if none) are consistent with the finalized prefix; each has its own once-only bitmap.

I7 Factories. Application address binds template, withdrawal configuration and all consensus settings; the consensus address binds the application. MultiLevelTournamentFactory.instantiate/instantiateInner are permissionless but a tournament counts only if DaveConsensus (root) or its parent (child) created it. Released geometry 54+38 = 24+48+20 = 92 matches CartesiStateTransition's masks and MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH.

I8 Recipe referee model (prt.lua wait_for_outputs, game-output.lua) agrees with the contracts on A5: three whole-machine word proofs against the settled hash, the same yield predicate, output proofs with log2_target_size 0, log2_root_size 63, index range check, keccak256(output) leaf, and verify_slice enforcing the sibling count. It runs one epoch, so its per-epoch accepted-index set cannot replay an output across epochs.
experiments: Largest InputBox input through the guest tools: with the in-tree emulator and the harness `valid-template` (Linux + machine-guest-tools v0.18.1-test1 rootfs, echo app using the `rollup` CLI), I delivered an EvmAdvance of 65,508 bytes (payload 65,216 bytes, the largest that InputBox's INPUT_MAX_SIZE = 65,536 admits) and a 100-byte one. Both ended in a manual yield with reason rx-accepted, a 32-byte tx-buffer root equal to the keccak frontier over the emitted notice, and a notice byte-identical to the ABI encoding of the payload (279,203,569 and 56,407,683 mcycles). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r9/SUBCONSENSUS/maxinput.lua
Constants of the outputs-root extraction (step 0.15.0 copy inside rollups-contracts) compared with the built emulator's Lua module: all equal (see I4).
notes: Not reported, same site and root cause as R1-A7-2 (refuted): the released root allowance (ClockBudgets.maxAllowance = censorship + 2 response budgets + one refill; 1 week + 2 h 20 min on mainnet) has no term for executing the sealed epoch, and DaveConsensus seals every pending input up to 2^24 at acceptance. R1-A7-2's trigger was a flood in the sealing block. A different trigger exists: a sustained flood at any rate above the honest operator's processing rate (the chain admits on the order of 100 inputs per second at about 27,500 gas per batched addInput) makes the operator's lag grow without bound, so some later seal hands it more unexecuted inputs than it can run before the root closes. If R1-A7-2 was refuted because one block cannot hold the flood, this trigger removes that ground; if it was refuted because execution capacity against the input rate is the deployment's sizing (A7, 'sizing the deployment for it is the deployment's job'), the same reading covers it. I leave the decision to triage and did not count it as a candidate.

Manual wording only, no behavior at stake: doc/README.md 'Output verification' says the three-word proof confirms 'that the machine accepted its last input'. After a rejected last input the settled canonical state is the pre-input state, so the proof shows that the settled state waits at an rx-accepted yield, not that the last input was accepted. Contracts, recipes and the threat model agree with each other; I did not rate it.
not_covered: No transaction was run on a chain: stageTournamentResult, acceptStagedTournamentResult, submitSentryClaim, rotateSentry, executeOutput, issueRefund, proveAccountsDriveMerkleRoot and withdraw were checked by reading the released sources only. No forge test, no anvil run, no gas measurement of the shell's own calls.

Dave's own knowledge base beyond docs/epoch-lifecycle.md and the two AGENTS.md files (docs/todo.md, docs/dimensioning.md, docs/dispute-game.md, docs/reviews/) was not read; docs/reviews and docs/todo.md were skipped on purpose as possible earlier review records.

Tournament internals that decide the root winner (pairing, clocks, timeouts, elimination, inner-result propagation, refunds): only tournamentStanding, joinTournament, winLeafMatch, the time predicates and Commitment.requireFinalState were read, as far as the consensus seam needs.

Delegate-call vouchers and vouchers that target the Application, DaveConsensus or the InputBox themselves (storage rewrite of the executed bitmap, the validator or the foreclosure flag) were treated as the application's own outputs and not pursued.

Portals (Ether, ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155), RefundOutputBuilder's deposit decoders for ERC-721/1155 and SelfHostedApplicationFactory, Authority and Quorum were skimmed or not read; Dave does not use the last three.
The deployed InputBox and ApplicationFactory come from the prebuilt deployments of cartesi-rollups-contracts; I audited the source, not that bytecode, and did not compare the two.

Chain-specific behavior: block.number on Arbitrum (parent-chain block) for onDeploymentBlock, the staging period and the tournament clocks; per-transaction limits of chains other than Ethereum for the 94 KB delivery proof.

The validator nodes' handling of the shell's events (Dave's Rust node, Cartesi Rollups Node) is out of scope; the PRT bridge and crisium (support) were read only for staging by a third party (stage job is skipped once EpochStaged is observed) and not re-audited.

Guest tools at the InputBox boundary beyond the one experiment: rollup-http-server and libcmt consumers other than the `rollup` CLI were not run with the largest input; rejected and exception paths were not run at that size.
vg.lua's dapp contract and output acceptance were only checked for being single-epoch.
